question.nlq: Could you tell me which patients would be classified as having antiphospholipid syndrome according to the current international diagnostic criteria based on their examination and laboratory results?

meanings.feedback: This question requires the application of the revised Sapporo/Sydney classification criteria for antiphospholipid syndrome (APS), which is external medical knowledge not stored in the database. The criteria require: (1) At least one clinical criterion (vascular thrombosis or pregnancy morbidity), AND (2) At least one laboratory criterion (positive aCL IgG/IgM above certain thresholds, positive anti-beta2-glycoprotein-I, or positive lupus anticoagulant) confirmed on two occasions at least 12 weeks apart. The database contains some relevant tests (aCL IgG, aCL IgM, LAC, KCT, RVVT, Thrombosis), but does NOT contain: (1) the specific threshold values for 'significant' antibody titers required by the classification criteria, (2) the timing requirement for repeat testing (12-week intervals between positive results), (3) the exact definition of qualifying thrombotic events per the criteria, (4) the relationship between different test types (+/- vs numerical values). Without these external diagnostic standards, no valid SQL query can determine APS classification.

SELECT DISTINCT e.ID
FROM Examination AS e
WHERE e.Thrombosis > 0
  AND (

turns.sql:
SELECT p.ID,
       CAST((julianday('now') - julianday(p.Birthday))/365.25 AS INTEGER) AS Age,
       (CASE WHEN e.`aCL IgG` >= 40 THEN 1 ELSE 0 END
        + CASE WHEN e.`aCL IgM` >= 40 THEN 1 ELSE 0 END
        + CASE WHEN e.LAC = '+' THEN 1 ELSE 0 END
        + CASE WHEN e.Thrombosis > 0 THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS RiskScore
FROM Patient p
JOIN Examination e ON p.ID = e.ID
WHERE (CASE WHEN e.`aCL IgG` >= 40 THEN 1 ELSE 0 END
        + CASE WHEN e.`aCL IgM` >= 40 THEN 1 ELSE 0 END
        + CASE WHEN e.LAC = '+' THEN 1 ELSE 0 END
        + CASE WHEN e.Thrombosis > 0 THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) >= 3
ORDER BY RiskScore DESC, p.ID;
